newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -gains hold in post-Fed trade.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -gains hold in post-Fed trade.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices mainly kept their gains in late trade on Wednesday after the Federal Reserve left interest rates unchanged, a decision that was widely expected.

"I think you could call it up a quarter of a point, most of that is from the intermediate (sector) to the long-end. High-grades were up about an 0.02," said a municipal analyst, who described activity as light to moderate.
Another trader said: "It's probably up a couple of basis points but there's really nothing going on. It's really just people squaring positions ahead of tomorrow's payrolls number."

The release of this major economic report, the June payrolls data, set for 0830 EDT on Thursday, and the minutes of a previous meeting of the central bank's policy making arm, were seen as some of the few reasons for traders to be at their desks ahead of the holiday.
Barring any surprises in those reports, trading was anticipated to slow even further, as the market will close early at 1500 EDT before the U.S. Independence Day holiday on Friday.

A trader added that while there were bids for attractively structured paper, dealers mainly had lightened inventories over the past few weeks, and looked to be heading into the crucial jobs data, which can shake markets, with fairly flat positions.
One of the recent features has been the continuing strong interest in New Jersey's $2.75 billion of taxable bonds, which were sold last week by its Economic Development Authority.

A trader speculated the bonds were drawing corporate buyers, who tend to make forays into the municipal area if there is an unusually attractive offering, and noted that the debt was pegged about 0.08 to 0.14 basis points above the initial prices.

In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, Airport Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5.4 percent coupon. They were bid at 5.74 percent, NET, down three basis points.
And Florida Ports Financing Commission Revenues of 2027, which pay a 5-3/8 percent coupon, were bid at 5.68 percent, NET, down two basis points.
September municipal futures ended up 20 ticks at 117-23/32, while September Treasury bond futures rose 14 ticks to 112-2/32. The MOB spread firmed slightly to plus 181 ticks.
